intro: You're a landlord looking for a bookkeeper near you who understands rental property records. You want someone local who can keep your rent, agent statements, repairs and mortgage costs in order, property by property. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK bookkeeper who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What landlords searching for a bookkeeper usually need
need_lead: Landlords often need help keeping clear, separate records for each property so that tax time is less stressful.
needs: You have rent coming in from several tenants and need each property's income recorded separately.
Letting agent statements arrive monthly and you want them reconciled against your bank account.
You have repair bills and maintenance costs that need to be matched to the right property.
You want to keep capital improvements separate from repairs so your tax records are clear.
You are unsure how to record mortgage costs and other expenses in a way that makes sense for your tax return.
context_heading: One key thing to understand about bookkeeping for landlords
context: Bookkeeping is not a regulated title in the UK, but anyone providing bookkeeping services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by HMRC or by a professional body. Membership of the Institute of Certified Bookkeepers (ICB) or the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) shows a bookkeeper has trained to a recognised standard and agreed to a code of conduct.

Ask whether a bookkeeper holds professional indemnity insurance and which body supervises them. Good bookkeepers are also clear about where their work stops and an accountant's starts, for example on year-end accounts and tax advice.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: How many properties you rent out and whether they are residential or commercial.
Whether you use letting agents and how often you receive statements from them.
What records you already keep and whether they are on paper, in a spreadsheet or in software.
Whether you want help with bookkeeping only or also with preparing information for your accountant.
Any particular concerns, such as keeping capital improvements separate from repairs.
Your preferred way of working with a bookkeeper, for example in person locally or remotely.
questions: Which body supervises you for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you separate records for each property?
How do you handle letting agent statements and reconcile them?
Where does your work stop and an accountant's begin?
What information do you need from me each month to keep my records up to date?

faqs.q: Do I need a bookkeeper if I already have an accountant?
faqs.a: Many landlords use a bookkeeper to keep day-to-day records in order and an accountant for year-end accounts and tax advice. A bookkeeper can take on the routine recording of rent, agent statements, repairs and mortgage costs, which can reduce the work passed to your accountant.

faqs.q: How do I find a bookkeeper near me who understands rental property?
faqs.a: Look for a bookkeeper who mentions experience with landlords and rental records, and ask how they keep each property separate. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK bookkeeper based on what you tell us, and they will quote you directly.

faqs.q: What records should I keep for each property?
faqs.a: Keep rent received, letting agent statements, repair and maintenance costs, and mortgage costs recorded separately for each property. It also helps to keep capital improvements separate from repairs, as they are treated differently for tax.

faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper help me get ready for my tax return?
faqs.a: A bookkeeper can keep your records organised and provide clear summaries, but tax advice and filing are usually the accountant's role. Ask the bookkeeper where their work stops and an accountant's begins so you know what to expect.

extra: Searching for a landlord bookkeeper near me suggests you'd value someone you can meet face to face, or at least reach easily by phone, to talk through rent, agent statements and repair bills property by property. Local knowledge can help when you want to hand over a folder of letting agent statements and talk through each property in person. It doesn't make for a better service on its own, so weigh convenience alongside how clearly the bookkeeper explains their approach.

When you compare bookkeepers, ask each one to walk you through how they would set up a separate record for every property, reconcile agent statements and keep capital improvements apart from repairs. A bookkeeper who asks sensible questions about your portfolio and is upfront about where their work stops and an accountant's begins is showing you how they think. Ask which body supervises them for anti-money-laundering purposes and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, then judge the answers for yourself rather than relying on a label.

At a first meeting, expect to talk through each property, your letting agents and the records you already hold, whether paper, spreadsheet or software. A good bookkeeper will explain what they need from you each month and how they will report back, and will be clear about the boundary with your accountant on year-end accounts and tax advice. Take your time, ask the same questions of more than one bookkeeper, and compare the quotes directly before deciding.

extra_faqs.q: Is a local landlord bookkeeper better than one working remotely?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. A local bookkeeper may suit you if you prefer to hand over paperwork in person, while a remote one can work just as well if your records are already digital. What matters is that they understand rental property records and are clear about how they will keep each property separate.

extra_faqs.q: Can a bookkeeper deal with my letting agent directly?
extra_faqs.a: Some bookkeepers will contact letting agents for statements, while others prefer you to pass the statements on. Ask at the outset how they would like to receive agent statements and how they will reconcile them against your bank account. Agreeing this early avoids confusion later.
